$comment: Generated by tools/ont-check/gen-contracts.mjs from the ontology. Do not edit by hand.

concept.title: Concept
concept.description: Something in the product that people talk about, with one permanent ID and one definition row.

id.description: class.name in lowercase; a field or a relation adds its entity, field.loan.due-date. Never changes.

kind.description: One of the classes the configuration lists, in the order rows are grouped; by default entity, field, relation, derived, concept, rule, invariant, hook, action, view.

term.description: The name people use. It may change; the ID does not.

type.description: For fields and relations: a type from the neutral vocabulary. For a view: shows and the entities it shows, by ID.

definition.description: What the concept is, in one or two sentences. Tooltips, reference pages and contracts quote it.

entity.description: The entity a field or relation belongs to, named in its ID.

retired-id.title: Retired ID
retired-id.description: An ID that had to change, kept so that the decision log, which is never edited, still resolves.

replacedBy.description: The concept that replaces it; none for a removed concept.

other-word.title: Other word
other-word.description: A word people may use for a concept that is not its term. It is listed so that the text a project writes uses the term instead.

word.description: The word or phrase, in the form it would be written; each form is a row of its own.

concept.description: The concept the word would stand for.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: One choice about the product, with its reason and the alternatives rejected.

status.description: Accepted entries are final; a tentative one may change without a new entry, and its acceptance is a line in History.

choice.description: What was chosen, precisely enough to implement.

why.description: The reason, including what went wrong before.

rejected.description: Each alternative with its reason in brackets.

title.description: One line that states the decision, not the topic: "No money fines", not "Fines".

source.description: Where the choice was made: a call with the time of the passage, a message with its date, the owner's answer to a question, a document by its path; named on a Source: line.

returnWhen.description: What must happen before what the entry puts off is taken up again; named on a Return when: line, it makes the entry a deferral.

layer.description: Product by default; process for an entry about how agents work rather than about the product, marked by a Layer: process line.

supersedes.description: Earlier entries this one replaces, each whole, named on a Supersedes: line; they are replaced once this entry is accepted.

extends.description: Rules of the approach that a process entry adds to for the project, named on an Extends: line.

overrides.description: Rules of the approach that a process entry changes for the project, named on an Overrides: line.

implementation-row.title: Implementation row
implementation-row.description: A claim that one or more concepts exist in the product, with the files and a note on what is partial.

files.description: Paths of the files that realise the concept.

concept.description: The concepts the row claims; concepts realised in the same files may share a row.

divergence.title: Divergence
divergence.description: A place where the product does something the target does not want.

description.description: What the product does instead, and the ticket or decision that will settle it.

mockup-element.title: Mockup element
mockup-element.description: A meaningful element of the mockup, labelled with a concept by data-ont.

concept.description: The concept the element stands for.

map-row.title: Map row
map-row.description: A row of the UI-to-ontology map: one mockup element and its concept.

shows.description: What the element shows, on this screen.

check.title: Check
check.description: A case with data that must hold for any implementation, in the product's terms.

proof.description: auto when a test implements it, judged when a test runs it and a model judges the output against its THEN, review when a reviewer of another provider gives it a verdict reading the change before merge, run when an agent runs it on the working product, in the mockup or blind, or a person where the project chooses so. auto and judged checks are automatic; review and run have no test, and a record of a verdict says who carried each out.

manual-run.title: Verdict record
manual-run.description: A record of a verdict on a check of review or run: one file in the directory the configuration names under verdicts.

time.description: When the verdict was given, in UTC to the second; it orders the records of a check.

commit.description: The commit or the range of commits the verdict was given on.

stamp.description: The stamp of the check's case, its proof and its concepts when the verdict was given, as --review prints it.

verdict.description: What the verdict found; not-run and not-applicable say why the check was not carried out.

by.description: Who gave the verdict: the reviewer, a model and its provider, or a person; one value for every record of a review.

performer.description: Who carried the check out, on a pass or a fail only: agent by default, person when the project gave the run to a person and the reviewer passes the result on, whose name is then in the evidence. A record without it is read as before.

evidence.description: Where the evidence is, outside the repository.

origin.description: Who wrote the record: review, the reviewer's verdict by --review --record, or run, a run of a check of run outside a review by --run-record; a record without the line is the reviewer's, as before.

check.description: The check the verdict is on, from the project's catalogue or the approach's.

review-round.title: Review round
review-round.description: One round of review of a task, with what it cost and what it found: one file in the directory the configuration names under reviewRounds.

task.description: The task the round belongs to, named the same in every round and step of it, in lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

step.description: Which review the round belongs to: of the task's statement or of its result.

narrow.description: Whether the round read only the fixes of the round before it.

number.description: The round's number among the rounds of its step in the task, the full rounds and the narrow ones counted apart.

time.description: When the round ended, in UTC to the second.

commits.description: The commit or the range of commits the round reviewed, its last commit the one reviewed; none for a review of a statement, and required of a round that gives a verdict of acceptance.

by.description: Who reviewed: a model and its provider, or a person.

tokensNew.description: The input tokens the round read that were not in a cache, as its provider reports them; left out when not known.

tokensCached.description: The input tokens the round read from a cache; left out when not known.

tokensOut.description: The tokens the round wrote; left out when not known.

checksListed.description: How many checks --review listed for the round.

checksGiven.description: How many of them got a new verdict in the round.

checksCarried.description: How many kept a verdict of an earlier round.

findings.description: One line for each finding: its class of problem, named the same in every round of the task; its weight, important or nit; whether it is of this change or was there before; whether it is fixable within the task, not fixable without changing what the owner decided, or filed as a limitation or for later (rule.findings-filed); and the test that holds its fix, once fixed, or the file it is filed in.

start.description: When the round began, in UTC to the second; given whenever the record names its contribution, and not after its time.

contribution.description: The run of a model the round was, by its provider and the ID of the session or task there, such as a thread or a delegated task: provider · ID.

acceptance.description: On a review of the result, the verdict of acceptance beside the verdict on merging: clean, or a finding line for each item of the approved statement, of its condition of done or of the owner's sources the result does not meet.

condition.description: On a review of the result, holds when the reviewer confirmed that the goal's condition by the approved statement is met: the reviewer's reply says Condition: holds or Condition: not yet, and the executor carries only holds into the record of the round; any other value, and the line on a review of the statement, is an error of the record (derived.next-round).

overspend.description: On the round that ends the task, what it spent past its budget with reserve, new input and output each, exactly as --task prints it, new input N of L, output N of L: the spend and the limit the tool computes, by the limits derived.task-budget gives, each number written one way, a whole number or a decimal with a point, such as 151.5; required past the limit and absent within it, by --task and the check alike. A round written with a snapshot of spend, Spend-record:, is compared with that snapshot's sums and limits, by --task and the check alike, so that CI, with no logs, and a later spend leave it as it was written (D-169). For a task of a goal past the goal's reserve, the goal's part follows, ; goal <goal>: new input N of L, output N of L; a goal itself, its own unit, is one sum against one set of limits and has the task's part alone, by the state of spend from the logs and by its snapshot alike (D-179).

briefTime.description: When round.mjs brief gave the round's brief, copied from it by round.mjs record; the start of the unit of budget is the earliest of them.

done.description: On a round of the result written by round.mjs record, the record of done it reviewed, whose commit Commits: gives.

spendRecord.description: The snapshot of spend round.mjs record wrote with the round, by its file name; the round's tokens are its sums of the round, and its Overspend: is compared with it.

gatePaths.description: On a round of the review of a statement, the statement's gate paths, Gate-paths: apart by , , which round.mjs record copies from the brief, so that a clean round approves them with the version it read (field.task-statement.gate-paths); the line on a round of the result is an error of the record (D-185).

cause.description: On a round briefed after stagnation, the SHA-256 of the file of the analysis of the cause the executor gave round.mjs brief with --cause, copied from the brief by round.mjs record; a round without it, as every round before it, reads as it did.

roundChecks.description: The line Round-checks: of a record of a round, once, the IDs of the checks of the record of a round its brief named, apart by , : the reader of rounds reads it, before the writer that writes it is merged, and gives it with the other fields of the round, deciding nothing by it; its meaning is set by the task that writes it, enforcement-verdicts-tests (D-186).

runs.description: The records of the verdicts the round gave, by file name.

statement.description: The version of the task's statement the round read, or checked the result against, by the SHA-256 of its file: the line Statement-hash:.

task-statement.title: Task statement
task-statement.description: What a task is to do, written before work on it starts: a file with the owner's sources for it, what to do and what not to do, its condition of done as commands and its budget. Its version is the SHA-256 of the file.

file.description: The path of the statement, given to the tool with --statement; the file may live outside the repository.

sources.description: Links to the owner's words the task rests on: his answers and messages.

todo.description: The items the result must meet.

notTodo.description: What the task must leave alone.

doneWhen.description: The commands that must pass on the result, one line Done-when: each.

budget.description: The task's own limits of new input and output tokens, on the lines Budget-new-input: and Budget-output:, and its reserve, the multiplier of the limits at which it stops, on the line Budget-reserve:, a number of 1 or more written as a whole number or a decimal with a point, such as 1.5, each in place of the project's default; a line given that cannot be read is named by --task.

goal.description: The goal the task is part of, on a line Goal: <goal>: its unit of budget where spend is counted from the logs. The unit of a task is the goal only when its statement names it so; a statement with no line is its own unit, with its own limits, and no error (D-179). The line is read from the statement file given, its line or its absence; with no file given, as in CI and round.mjs record, from the records of the version that applies (derived.task-budget) that copy the statement's lines of the budget, the task's kept brief of that version, or else its latest record of done of it, or else its latest snapshot of spend of it, whose Unit: is the goal where it is not the task, by the record's line or its absence, so that a version with no line is its own unit whatever an older version named; only where no record of that version copies those lines, as for a version whose only record is the owner's approval, from the latest of the task's records of another version that carries a line; with no line there the task is its own unit (D-179). The configuration lists each goal's tasks under goals, its composition: a line that names a goal the configuration does not list, or a goal whose list does not hold the task, is an error of --task, round.mjs and done.mjs, and a record of done or a kept brief whose line is so is an error of the check; a task listed under two goals is an error. The commands of a goal, --task <goal>, the goal's record of done and the brief of its acceptance, count it whole by that composition, its tasks whose statements have no line included.

gatePaths.description: The gate paths the task may change, in the syntax of mergeGate.paths, on one or more lines Gate-paths:, apart by commas or spaces. The approval of the version carries them: round.mjs brief of a round of the statement's review and approve.mjs --kind approval copy them into the brief, the round and the record of approval, and the guard, which reads no statement, reads them there (inv.gate-path-in-approval); a version with no line allows no gate path (D-185).

owner-approval.title: Owner approval
owner-approval.description: The owner's approval of one version of a task's statement, given in his own words, as when a finding of its review goes to him: one file in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, Record: approval.

task.description: The task, named as in its rounds of review.

by.description: owner: only the owner's approval is recorded so.

source.description: The owner's words or his answer that approve the version, with the date.

time.description: When the approval was given, in UTC to the second.

kind.description: approval, the owner's approval of the version, or gate, his answer to the gate of the round it names, which closes that gate alone, the other gates staying open, and approves no version (derived.approval); publish is the owner's permission to publish (ent.publish-permission), no approval of a version either; a record without the line is an approval (D-185).

question.description: The number of the question of the registry whose answer the record carries.

round.description: For an answer to a gate, the file of the round whose gate it closes.

budget.description: The limits and the reserve of the version the record names, as approve.mjs copies them from the lines Budget-new-input:, Budget-output: and Budget-reserve: of its statement, as done.mjs does, each a number or none, so that a record of the approval is a record of that version for derived.task-budget; a record written before these lines carries none and reads as before (D-179).

gatePaths.description: On an approval, the gate paths of the version it approves, Gate-paths: apart by , , as approve.mjs copies them from the statement's lines (field.task-statement.gate-paths); none where the statement has none (D-185).

statement.description: The version approved, by the SHA-256 of its file.

publish-permission.title: Publish permission
publish-permission.description: The owner's permission to publish the work of a goal or of a task, in his own words: one file <time>-<scope>-publish.md in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, Record: approval with Kind: publish; no approval of a version of a statement, and it names none.

scope.description: A goal of the configuration's goals, whose tasks and pull requests of records alone it covers, or a task, which it covers alone.

question.description: The number of the question of the registry whose answer the record carries; the question names the scope.

by.description: owner: only the owner allows to publish.

source.description: The number of the question, the date of the answer, the option chosen, whose value is publish, and the English translation of the owner's words, marked translated from Russian.

time.description: When the record was written, in UTC to the second.

guard.description: The gate whose guard reads the permission, on the base of a pull request or added by it, for the merge by the state of the task (rule.merge-by-task-state).

task-result.title: Task result
task-result.description: The executor's record of done: the task, the commit of its result, the version of the approved statement, the commands of done with their results on that commit and, where the statement asks the record to name more, its evidence, one file in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords.

task.description: The task, named as in its rounds of review; it names the file of the record, so it is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

commit.description: The commit of the result, in full.

budget.description: The statement's own limits and reserve, as done.mjs copies them from its lines Budget-new-input:, Budget-output: and Budget-reserve:, each a number or none; a reader given no file of that version reads its limits from them by derived.task-budget, and --task refuses the latest record of done of its statement's file's version whose limits or reserve are not the file's; a record of done of another version is not compared with the file. With them, the statement's goal, Goal:, where it names one, from which a reader given no file reads the scope of the budget, held to the configuration's goals (field.task-statement.goal, D-179). A record made before these lines carries none, and one made before the line of the reserve carries no reserve.

checks.description: Each command of done with its result, pass or fail.

evidence.description: What the approved statement asks the record of done to name besides the commands of done, such as each row of the catalogue the task changed, one line each under a line Evidence: after the checks, as done.mjs --evidence FILE copies them from the file's lines that are not blank; a reviewer of acceptance reads it there. Where the configuration sets records.latinOnly, its lines hold only English text and paths of the repository, as a record of a gate change does (rule.records-english-in-repo): done.mjs refuses such a file and writes nothing, and the check refuses a record of done whose evidence does not, naming the letter or the path and its line. A record made without it carries none (D-166).

time.description: When the commands had run, in UTC to the second.

statement.description: The version of the statement the result answers, by the SHA-256 of its file.

task-spend.title: Task spend
task-spend.description: The executor's own work on a task in one run of a model, without the sessions of reviewers, which their rounds record: one file in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords.

contribution.description: The run, by its provider and the ID of the session or task there: provider · ID; the interval is not part of it.

start.description: When the run began on the task, in UTC to the second.

end.description: When it ended, no earlier than its start.

tokensNew.description: The input tokens it read that were not in a cache; left out when not known.

tokensCached.description: The input tokens it read from a cache, which no budget counts.

tokensOut.description: The tokens it wrote; left out when not known.

task.description: The task the work was for, named as in its rounds.

merge-gate.title: Merge gate
merge-gate.description: The server's refusal to merge into main a pull request whose required checks did not pass on its head, or whose branch does not contain main: a ruleset of the repository on GitHub, with the two checks it requires, which no agent can skip as it can skip a hook of its clone.

fullCheck.description: The workflow ont-check, run on pull_request with a read-only token: the check of the approach, of the example and of the templates, the guard of decisions against the pull request's base, which fails when that base is not a commit it finds, and every test suite npm test runs but the judged; it runs the pull request's code.

guard.description: The workflow ont-gate-guard, run on pull_request_target, so that its definition and its code are main's: it fetches the pull request's commits as data, reads the paths the diff between the merge base of the event's base and its head changes and the records at that head, with the files at that head a filed finding may name (rule.findings-filed), so that a version is approved in force for it as for --task, runs nothing of the pull request and writes none of it into the working tree; it has a read-only token and no secret, and runs again on each push; its last step, which runs whatever the guard found, compares the rules of main on GitHub with the rule file, the fields that token reads (inv.rules-match-file). A Git command of it that fails is an error that refuses the pull request, never a diff or a history without changes.

gatePaths.description: The paths of the repository whose change could weaken the gate, listed in the configuration under mergeGate.paths: a path ending in / names everything under it, and * any name within one part of a path.

ruleFile.description: The file of the repository that the configuration names under mergeGate.rules, holding the ruleset of main as the GitHub API takes it and the permissions of Actions the gate needs, so that the settings on GitHub can be compared with it.

ciWorkflow.description: The workflow file of a project's full check, which its configuration names under ci.workflow from its root; the templates give one.

taskState.description: The key mergeGate.taskState of the configuration: where the configuration at the base of a pull request sets it, the guard holds the merge by the state of the task (rule.merge-by-task-state), reading the composition of the goals, goals, from that base too; the pull request that brings the key is not held by it, and the next one is (D-185).

driftWorkflow.description: The workflow ont-rules-drift, run on main once a day and on demand with a read-only token, even when the rule of pull requests is taken off: it compares the rules of main on GitHub with the rule file, every field its token reads, and says each one it cannot read (inv.rules-match-file).

changes.description: The records of gate changes the guard reads at the head of a pull request.

gate-change.title: Gate change
gate-change.description: The record, in a pull request, that a change of gate paths is the work of a task under an approved version of its statement: one file <time>-<task>-gate-change.md in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, Record: gate-change.

task.description: The task whose statement allows the change, named as in its rounds.

item.description: The item of What to do of that version that allows the change.

paths.description: The gate paths the change makes, one per line, each a path of the repository.

commit.description: The commit, in full, at which the pull request's change of the paths the record lists is whole: the last commit of the pull request that changes a path outside reviews/, never a later commit of records alone; each of them changes between the merge base and it; the record is added by the next commit, whose one parent it is, and after it the pull request changes nothing outside reviews/ but by merging main.

time.description: When the record was written, in UTC to the second.

statement.description: The approved version of the statement, by the SHA-256 of its file.

gate-proof.title: Gate proof
gate-proof.description: The record of a live probe of a gate on GitHub: one file <time>-<task>-gate-proof.md, named by the task whose gate it probes, in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, Record: gate-proof.

kind.description: A refusal is proven by an attack the gate refused; a pass by an ordinary merge through it.

probe.description: pr <number> for a pull request, push <ref> for a push.

result.description: What GitHub did with the attempt; a proof counts only when it agrees with its kind.

refusedBy.description: For a refusal, the check or the rule whose answer refused it, so that the proof is of this gate and not of an earlier one.

head.description: For a pull request, the commit of its head, in full.

base.description: For a pull request, the commit of main it was based on when its checks ran, in full: for a pass, the first parent of its merge commit, which the branch being up to date with main makes the main its checks ran against, and an ancestor of its head; for a refusal, read before main moves on and given to the writer, or else read while the pull request is open; for a refusal for being behind, read before main moves on.

mainAfter.description: For a refusal for being behind, the commit main moved on to, read after it moved, in full; it is not the base.

check.description: For a pull request, the check that ran on its head and its result, <name> · <result>.

run.description: For a pull request, the number of the run of that check and its address, <number> · <URL>.

required.description: For a pull request, the required check and its result, <name> · <result>.

answer.description: For a refusal, GitHub's answer to the attempt to merge or to push.

merge.description: For a pass, the commit of the merge, in full.

time.description: When the probe was made, in UTC to the second.

gate.description: The task whose gate was probed, named as in its rounds, on the line Gate:.

process-record.title: Process record
process-record.description: A record of the process that a writer of the tool writes: a round of review, a verdict, a record of done, the owner's approval, answer to a gate or permission to publish, a snapshot of spend, a record of fixes, a gate change or a gate proof; a file in the directory of rounds, of verdicts or of task records the configuration names.

seal.description: The first line of the record, Seal: v1 <sha256>: the SHA-256 of the prefix of its format, ont-check seal v1, a line feed and the rest of the file. It depends on the format and not on the version of the tool, so the guard of main and a writer on a branch compute it alike; a later format is v2, and v1 is still read.

sealsFrom.description: The key records.sealsFrom of the configuration: where the configuration at the base of a pull request sets it, a record the pull request adds whose Time: is after the committer time of the commit of the base's first-parent history that brought the key in, its merge into main, needs a valid seal; a record before it, in the base or on the branch of the task that brought the key, reads as before.

refusalCode.description: What the guard prints on a line CODE <code>, once for each rule a pull request breaks: GATE_PATH_UNAPPROVED, SEAL_MISSING, SEAL_WRONG, RECORD_CHANGED and RECORD_REMOVED; where field.merge-gate.task-state is set at the base, TASK_UNNAMED, TASK_NOT_DONE, TASK_HEAD_UNREVIEWED, WORK_BEFORE_APPROVAL, MERGE_UNPERMITTED (rule.merge-by-task-state) and GATE_PATH_OUTSIDE_APPROVAL (inv.gate-path-in-approval); and from the comparison of the rules on GitHub, RULES_DRIFT and RULES_UNREAD (inv.rules-match-file); the configuration lists under mergeGate.codes the codes of each task's gate, which a gate proof of a refusal compares with the output of the check.

guard.description: The gate whose guard refuses a record of the process written by hand, edited or removed.

round-brief.title: Round brief
round-brief.description: The brief of one round of review that round.mjs brief gives: its lines, kept once in ont-briefs/ of the Git directory of the working copy, never in the tree, so that a linked worktree keeps its own; the executor puts them first in the reviewer's brief, and the reviewer's reply begins with them word for word.

lines.description: Task:, Step:, Narrow:, Number:, Statement-hash:, Goal: where the statement names one, from which a reader given no file reads the scope of the budget, held to the configuration's goals (field.task-statement.goal, D-179), Budget-new-input:, Budget-output: and Budget-reserve:, the statement's limits and reserve, each a number or none, the limits of the brief's version, which round.mjs record reads by derived.task-budget for that version, whatever version is approved in force, for a round of the review of a statement that has them, Gate-paths:, its gate paths, which round.mjs record copies into the round (field.review-round.gate-paths, D-185), Commits:, for a round of the result Done:, the record of done it reviews, whose commit Commits: gives, on a round briefed after stagnation Cause:, the SHA-256 of the analysis of the cause given with --cause (field.review-round.cause), and Brief-time:, when the brief was given.

round.description: The round whose record round.mjs record writes from the brief and the reviewer's reply.

statement.description: The version of the statement the round reads, by the SHA-256 of its file.

fixes-record.title: Fixes record
fixes-record.description: The record of the fixes of the findings of one round, in one of two forms, the tests that hold them, or the one issue of verdicts after the narrow round (field.fixes-record.issue) with or without tests, never neither, in the closed grammar its writers emit: an optional line Seal:, the fields Record:, Task:, Round:, Time: and Issue:, each once, then the blocks Tests:, Issue-findings: and Filed:, each once with its lines - …, and no other line, no heading and no notes; Tests: is required unless a valid Issue: is given, Issue-findings: and Filed: are given only with Issue:, and a line of Filed: is limitation or later: Record: fixes, one file <time>-<task>-fixes.md in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, with its seal.

round.description: The round whose findings it tests, by its file on Round:.

tests.description: Under Tests:, one line for each class of a fixable finding of that round, word for word, with the file and the name of its test, - class · file · name; the reader of rounds takes the test of a finding from it when the round's record gives none, so that derived.next-round sees the fix held, and the record of the round is never changed. It may be left out only where the record names a valid Issue: (field.fixes-record.issue): a record of fixes holds valid tests, a valid issue or both, never neither, and a valid issue excuses no line under Tests: that is not - class · file · name with a path of the repository (D-186).

issue.description: The line Issue: of a record of fixes, a commit of seven to forty hexadecimal characters: the one issue of verdicts after the narrow round. The reader of records of fixes reads it before the writer that writes it is merged, and a record with a valid issue may give no line under Tests:; its meaning is set by the task that writes it, enforcement-verdicts-tests (D-186).

spend-snapshot.title: Spend snapshot
spend-snapshot.description: The spend of a unit of budget at the time a writer ran: Record: spend-snapshot, one file <time>-<task>-spend-snapshot.md in the directory the configuration names under taskRecords, which round.mjs record writes with its round.

unit.description: The unit of budget, Unit:: the goal the statement names on Goal:, or the task; and Unit-start:, when the unit began.

sums.description: New input, cached input and output, each a whole number, of the unit, of the task and of the round: Unit-new:, Unit-cached:, Unit-out:, the same with Task- and Round-.

limits.description: The limits and the reserve the sums were compared with, of the unit and of the task, with the versions of the statements they are of, the goal's approved version and, for the task, the version that applies to the writer, a round's brief's (derived.task-budget): Unit-limit-new:, Unit-limit-out:, Unit-reserve:, Unit-statement-hash:, the same with Task-, each a number or none.

round.description: The round it was written with, which names it on Spend-record:.

task.description: The task whose writer wrote it, named as in its rounds.

test.title: Test
test.description: Code that implements checks and starts its title with their IDs.

suite.description: The suite the test belongs to.

test-suite.title: Test suite
test-suite.description: A kind of test the team runs, such as unit or end-to-end, and the classes it must prove.

cover.description: The classes whose implemented concepts the suite must prove.

checks.description: Checks the suite must implement, such as a key scenario end to end or the checks a judge decides.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: A slice of the gap: what to build now, within which limits.

whyNow.description: Why this slice comes before the rest of the gap.

outOfScope.description: What not to build, though it is target too.

preAuthorized.description: Permissions the agent would otherwise stop and ask for.

checks.description: The checks of the slice, on the ticket's Checks: line.

dependsOn.description: Slices that must be done first.

agent-rules.title: Agent rules
agent-rules.description: The section of the agents' instructions that says what else to update when something changes, and what to run.

files.description: The files that hold the agents' instructions, listed in the configuration under agentInstructions; the check reads the IDs and entries they mention.

sources.description: The entries the instructions name as the source of their rules.

contract.title: Contract
contract.description: A JSON Schema per entity, generated from the types of its fields and relations.

entity.description: The entity whose fields and relations the schema describes.

doc-section.title: Doc section
doc-section.description: A hand-written section of a page for people, anchored to what it explains.

stamp.description: A short hash of what the section relies on for each concept it explains, the term, type, definition and the notes that name it, as it was when the section was last reread.

explains.description: The concepts and checks the section explains.

set.description: The doc set the page belongs to.

doc-set.title: Doc set
doc-set.description: A set of pages for one audience, and the classes or checks it must explain.

cover.description: The classes whose concepts the set must explain.

scope.description: Whether the set explains what is built or the whole target.

checks.description: The proofs whose checks the set must name in its anchors, run for a run guide; the earlier manual asks for the checks of run and those whose proof is still manual.

files.description: The pages of the set, named one by one, when they are not every page under one directory; a README named here is read like any other page.

reference-page.title: Reference page
reference-page.description: A page that only restates the ontology and the checks, generated, never edited.

ontology-tree.title: Ontology tree
ontology-tree.description: A page for people that shows the whole ontology as a tree: each entity with the rows of its table by kind, and a table without an entity under its heading. Written by a generator when someone wants to see the ontology, and by the protocol's hook after a merge into main in a clone that names its place; never kept in the repository.

place.description: Where a clone keeps its tree: a path in the clone's own Git configuration, ont.treeOut, never in ont.config.json, so that no path of one machine reaches the repository. Without it, no tree is refreshed and none is reported stale. The place is the file of its name in its directory as the file system resolves that directory, links and .. on the way followed; a place whose directory does not exist is refused. That file is refused with the reason, and nothing is written, when it lies inside a working tree of the repository, any of them, or its Git directory, so that a wrong setting never overwrites a file of the repository; when it is a symbolic link; when it is not a regular file; or when it has more than one link, which may be a file of the repository under another name. The page is written to a new file in that directory and renamed over the place, never into the file that is there, so that a link elsewhere to the old file keeps its bytes. The stale report reads the same file.

builtFrom.description: What the page was written from, in its mark: one footer in the one form the generator writes, its text saying in the generator's own words what its attributes say, the last element of the page, directly before the </body></html> that ends it with nothing but white space between, with the SHA-256 of the page's bytes before it and of the footer's commit, configuration and date, so that the mark is of the page the generator wrote with that footer, whose footer a person sees; with the commit of HEAD, read once; the path of the configuration from the root of the repository, except outside Git; and the date and time in UTC, to the second, such as 2026-11-20T09:30:00Z. An input's path is the one the configuration gives, never normalised; a .. part on it, or a part of it, the file included, that is a symbolic link or is missing, makes it not the commit's file. The refresh builds the page from the files of that commit, and only when the working tree holds the same at those paths, so its mark is that commit. A page written on demand reads each file of the working tree once, a regular file only, and is marked +working-tree when the bytes read are not the commit's file at the same path inside the repository, or when its path is not the commit's file when the file is read or after; outside Git it is marked no-commit.

concepts.description: The definition rows the tree shows.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: A recipe for a property of the product that its ontology shows: what to configure, what is required and what is recommended.

section.description: The section of the profiles page that holds the recipe.

tool-copy.title: Tool copy
tool-copy.description: A project's copy of tools/ont-check, without its tests, and of the approach's LICENSE, from one commit of the approach, in a directory of its own.

pin.description: The file that names the commit of the copy, its date, the last decision of the approach at that commit and the hash of every file, and lists the files the project keeps in the copy's directory as its own.

copyInfo.description: A file in the copy's directory, copy.json, that pin.mjs update writes and lists as the project's own in the pin, naming the commit of the approach the copy came from; the copied files are not changed.

approachClone.description: The local clone of the approach that a clone of the project names in its own Git configuration, git config --local ont.approachClone <path>, to learn of releases without the network.

lastDecision.description: The approach's last decision at the commit of the copy, which the pin names.

protocol-release.title: Protocol release
protocol-release.description: A version of the approach: an entry of releases.md with its version, its date and its verified commit, the commit its checks passed on, and an annotated tag v and the version on the release commit, a child of the verified commit that only adds the entry. The tag v0.1, made before releases were recorded, is the starting point, read as 0.1.0, with no entry.

version.description: The version in Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, three numbers, greater than every release before it.

verified.description: The commit the tests and the check passed on, in full; the parent of the release commit.

changes.description: The entries of the decision log between the verified commit of the release before, or the commit of v0.1, and this one's; derived from the log, never written by hand.

product-release.title: Product release
product-release.description: A version of a product made with the approach: a file in the directory the configuration names under releases, with its version, its commit, the hash of the pin of the protocol there, the checks run with their results, the version of the tool and the date.

version.description: The version in Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, unique among the releases; it names the record's file, <version>.md, which no other record's file is named.

commit.description: The commit released, in full, in the project's history.

checks.description: The checks run on the commit, the project's check and each test suite of the configuration at that commit, each with its result: pass when every test passed, skipped with how many when tests were skipped and none failed, or not run when no test ran, both for a test suite only, or fail; the project's check passes or fails.

tool.description: The version of the tool that ran the checks, as the release action writes it and the check compares it: the commit of the approach the pin at the release's commit names, or that commit itself when the pin names none, as the approach's own example has; a full commit. It says which tool the release's commit carries, not that the tool ran (rule.intact-is-not-run).

pin.description: The pin of the protocol at the commit, by the SHA-256 of the file that releases.pin of the configuration at that commit names, a file at that commit: a directory or anything else at the path is refused, never hashed.

deployment.title: Deployment
deployment.description: A release put into an environment at a time, recorded in the directory of the releases in a file whose name is not a version's; optional, since not every product is deployed.

environment.description: Where the release was put, such as staging or production.

time.description: When, in UTC to the second.

release.description: The release deployed, by its version.

formal-form.title: Formal form
formal-form.description: The behavior of a definition row in the form language: how a derived value or a rule is computed, what an invariant refuses, what an action or a hook does.

concept.description: The row whose behavior the form states; the form starts with its ID.

trace.title: Trace
trace.description: A check's case as steps the oracle runs: the GIVEN and the WHEN as actions and days, the THEN as outcomes, notifications and assertions.

check.description: The check whose case the trace runs.
